groups.trust_reason: Agent, memory, tool and routing behaviour is decided by the kernel under labels and grants; every surface renders the same state and none may add a privileged shortcut.
Interface features over the kernel; the browser is the screen and the page is untrusted for approvals, with the same views inside the desktop shell.
Needs the OS keychain, signed auto-update, local processes, isolated VMs, screen or microphone under native consent, which a browser cannot grant or enforce.
Account, billing, sharing or marketplace concerns that need a shared service; claimable only after hosted-mode isolation, keys and honest wording are validated.
Controlling the user's browser needs the extension adapter with narrow permissions and an origin allowlist; pages stay untrusted.
Core security and proof machinery; by definition one implementation shared by every surface so that boundaries, approvals and evidence agree under hostile tests.
Platform isolation, trusted approval and signed distribution depend on the operating system and are claimed per platform only after that platform passes its own isolation tests.
User-facing hardening and workflows rendered through the local companion with a strict content policy and an isolated viewer; the page is untrusted.
Reproducibility package, rooms and public log anchoring involve outside parties and published artifacts, with fixtures clearly labelled.
An embeddable policy kernel is a developer SDK consumed by other agents through stable typed schemas.
Scope-limited zero-knowledge calculation is a research go/no-go; no claim until a verified construction exists.
